mainEntity.name: How do I choose the right glass thickness for my shower enclosure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choosing the right glass thickness depends on the type of enclosure and desired stability. Frameless shower doors typically require thicker glass, such as 3/8-inch or 1/2-inch, to ensure structural integrity without a frame. Framed and semi-frameless enclosures can use thinner glass, like 1/4-inch, as the frame provides support. A thicker glass provides a more luxurious feel and superior sound dampening. Hometelligent can guide you through these options, ensuring your choice meets safety standards and your aesthetic preferences.
acceptedAnswer.description: Glass thickness depends on the enclosure type; frameless needs thicker glass (3/8"-1/2"), while framed can use thinner (1/4"). Thicker glass offers more stability and a luxurious feel.
